name: Warli

lumenary.blurb: White rice-paste drawings on a mud wall, from Maharashtra: triangles for bodies, circles for heads, and a crowd that gathers where your picture is darkest.

why: Warli painting is made with a vocabulary of three shapes: a circle, a triangle and a square, which are said to come from the sun and the moon, from mountains and trees, and from a field or a hut. A person is two triangles meeting at their tips with a circle for a head and stick limbs, and a crowd of them dances in a ring. The picture decides where the crowd gathers.

Place candidate positions on a staggered grid with spacing 0.82 u (u is the figure size), each shifted by up to a quarter of the spacing.
At each position let the picture’s tone t set the chance that anything is drawn: p = min(1, 1.15 d (1 − t)^1.5), where d is the crowd slider. Dark places hold a thick crowd and light ones stay empty.
Draw the figures in white rice paste: dancers, animals, trees and huts, with slightly wobbly lines.

history: Warli painting belongs to the Warli people, an Adivasi community of Maharashtra and Gujarat. It is painted on the red-brown mud walls of houses, in white rice paste, with a bamboo stick, and is often made for weddings, around a square drawn for the goddess Palaghata. In the 1970s the artist Jivya Soma Mashe brought Warli painting onto cloth and paper, and received a Padma Shri in 2011.
terms: An Adivasi community of western India, and its painting.
The white paint made of ground rice used on the mud walls.
paragraphs: Warli painting belongs to the Warli people of Maharashtra and Gujarat. It is painted on the red-brown mud walls of houses, in white rice paste, with a bamboo stick, and is often made for weddings. The vocabulary is small: a circle, a triangle and a square, said to come from the sun and the moon, mountains and trees, and a field or a hut. A human is two triangles meeting at their tips, with a circle for a head and stick limbs, and a crowd of them dances in a ring. The program fills the wall with such figures and lets the picture decide where the crowd gathers.

The wall is a texture of two noises, a broad one 90 px across and a fine one 5 px across. Candidate positions lie on a staggered grid with spacing 0.82 u (u is the figure size), each shifted by a random amount of up to a quarter of the spacing. At each position the picture’s tone t sets the chance that anything is drawn there: p = min(1, 1.15 d (1 − t)^1.5), where d is the crowd slider. Dark places therefore hold a thick crowd and light places stay empty. What is drawn is chosen at random: a figure 60% of the time, a tree 16%, a bird 10%, a hut 10% and a sun 4%. Its size also follows the picture, from 0.8 u in light places to 1.2 u in dark. A border of two frames and a chain of triangles is added when it is switched on.

equations.note: The chance that a grid position holds a drawing, from the tone t and crowd slider d.
The expected number of drawings in an area A.
The size of a figure, from the tone.
The pick, with h a random number fixed by the position and the seed. Figures are drawn from the top of the wall down so lower ones overlap higher ones.

presets.text: A full crowd fills the darkest parts of your picture.
Ochre walls feel like a sun-baked village.
A night wall makes the white figures glow.
